source_type: Treasury Decision 9123 final regulations, published May 3, 2004
scope: All 13 numbered/unnumbered examples within section 1.1296-1 in TD 9123 inventoried. Not an audit of every PFIC regulation.

examples.scenario: Unreversed inclusions: $150 cost, $240 value, $90 transition gain
examples.limits: Dollar facts retained; integration years 2005/06/07 shifted to 2021/22/23. Interest excluded from basis/inclusions.
Exact primitive; engine PFIC/election year shifted to 2023; no step-up to $1,100.
No annual PFIC-status history; do not submit cessation facts under the continuous-PFIC input contract.
Exact primitive and date-adapted engine integration.
No annual PFIC-status history; ordinary-loss primitive is not valid for this example.
Engine exports $100 other loss; capital character/holding-period reporting remains outside program.

examples.scenario: Two lots; $300 inclusion; $200 blocked decline; identified second-lot $100 loss
examples.limits: Year-end basis and inclusions tested end-to-end. Specific identification sale tested as a primitive only. Separate FIFO variant expects $100 ordinary gain selling first lot, not $100 loss.

examples.scenario: Partnership inside/outside basis and partner-specific allocations
examples.limits: Direct individual ownership only; cannot encode partnership ownership in current schema.

examples.scenario: Immigration dual basis and subsequent ordinary/capital sale split
examples.limits: Pre-residency input is rejected before valuation/calculation; no claim of supporting dual basis.

examples.scenario: QEF to MTM; loss of marketability terminates election
examples.limits: QEF and election termination history not implemented.
Election interruption and re-election not implemented.

examples.scenario: $10 transition deemed sale and basis increase
examples.limits: Original 1992/2005 allocation primitive; engine year shifted to 2023. Example specifies only excess: $100 basis/$110 value explicit test normalization. No official numeric interest result supplied.

examples.scenario: RIC shareholder special transition interest rule
examples.limits: Individual shareholder scope. Owning a mutual fund does not make the individual a RIC taxpayer.

rule_derived_tests: 1.1296-1(a)(3): subsequent decline limited by full prior transition inclusion
other_limits: Marketability and valid election remain explicitly confirmed inputs; 1.1296-2 marketability examples are not automatically evaluated.
1992 proposed 1.1291-2 distribution regulations are not represented as final Treasury regulations or as validated examples here.
Historical form years outside 2018-2025 remain unsupported; pure mathematical tests do not extend form-year support.
Cessation/partnership/QEF/RIC facts are not represented in the input schema. These are documented exclusions, not automatic detection/rejection tests.
Existing Andrew Mitchel interest discrepancies and taxpayer-specific due-date review remain unresolved; this suite does not certify filing readiness.
